text:
maria: heads-up — I prototyped an approach for the rerank endpoint to reduce token/quota waste for large candidate sets by deferring heavy prefetch/scoring into "priority slices". idea: send a cheap first-pass for 100s of candidates, pick top-k_small, then run the full scorer only on those.

maria: this would let us bill/route the initial pass at a lower unit and only incur full-cost model invocations on the compact slice. also helps with KV cache locality. :seedling:

aj: curious — how would this interact with existing quota accounting? do we double-charge a request (cheap pass + full pass)?

simon: short answer: depends on how we define units. we can treat the two passes as separate sub-requests with own units and aggregate for tenant billing, or we can expose a single logical request that maps to two internal calls but shows combined units in dashboard.

leah: from ops POV we need clear telemetry to surface where cost came from. if internal passes are opaque, it's impossible to debug spikes. need per-pass telemetry + correlation id.

maria: agreed. prototype includes a correlation header `X-RERANK-SLICE-ID` that ties both calls. snippet: ```http
POST /v1/rerank?mode=priority-slices
X-RERANK-SLICE-ID: 1729009999-1
{ "candidates": [...], "slice_policy": { "initial_limit": 250, "final_limit": 20 } }
```

devex-rachel: console UX question — do we expose `slice_policy` to users or keep it internal with a toggle? exposing gives power but confuses PLG users.

simon: propose two layers: default (managed) and advanced (user-controlled). managed mode picks sensible defaults and shows estimated unit breakdown in the request preview. advanced allows explicit slice sizes.

aj: SLA risk: some clients will need deterministic latency for the final score. adding a 2-stage flow could add tail latency if we don't pipeline correctly. can we run the full scorer on the highest-confidence subset concurrently with the cheap pass to avoid serial tails?

maria: yes, we can opportunistically pipeline: kick off best-effort scoring on first N prioritized candidates while initial pass finishes. if results overlap, we cancel redundant work. infra-bot: queued job 76342 created for simon/maria to benchmark pipeline cost savings.

leah: telemetry checklist for MVP: per-slice counts, per-pass P95 latency, units consumed per-pass, cancellation rates, correlation ids. need dashboard tiles and an alert if per-request units > threshold.

devex-rachel: for console, propose a toggle with tooltip: "Deferred prefetch (saves cost for large candidate sets; may affect tail latency)." also show estimated cost delta and a link to rollout playbook.

simon: canary plan: enable managed slices for 5% of traffic on non-critical tenants, sample full traces. if cost savings >= 20% and tail P99 < control + 50ms, widen.

aj: one more: fallback behavior. if the initial pass fails or times out, should we fall back to single-pass full scoring? i prefer fail-open to single-pass to preserve correctness.

maria: agree — default fallback = full-pass (single invocation) with a flag `fallback=single_pass`. will add `fallback` to API header.

leah: owner + action items?

maria: i'll own the RFC + proto. simon/aj to run bench and pipeline experiments. devex-rachel will mock console toggle and preview mockups. leah to define telemetry dashboard and alerts. target: small RFC and canary in 3 sprints. :v:

devex-rachel: I'll add a mock to the product board and link to the RFC when ready.

maria: cool, thanks all. leaving notes in the rerank RFC doc and pinging when prototype is up.
